```{r setup, include = FALSE}
                      fig.path = "output/figures/", dev = "png", dpi = 300,
                      # knitr appends -1 to the chunk name; drop it
                      fig.process = function(f) {

                        if (f != g) file.rename(f, g)
                        g

```

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse); library(sf); library(terra); library(marmap)
library(patchwork); library(rnaturalearth); library(ggspatial)

dir_derived <- "data/derived"; dir_fig <- "output/figures"
dir.create(dir_fig, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

BOX     <- list(lon = c(-98, -80), lat = c(18, 31))   # study area
MAP_LAT <- c(23.5, 31)                                # map extent, trimmed north of the Yucatan
SHELF_M <- 200                                        # shelf cut-off, metres
PEAK    <- c(6, 7)                                    # spawning-season months
SERIES  <- 1982:2016                                  # June-July sampling ends with the 2016 survey
SORTED  <- c("1", "2", "4", "D")
DWH     <- tibble(lon = -88.3660, lat = 28.7366)      # Deepwater Horizon wellhead

SIZE_LEVELS <- c("Small (<5 mm)", "Medium (5-15 mm)", "Large (>15 mm)")
# Size classes are ordered, so they run light to dark along viridis.
SIZE_COLS   <- c("Small (<5 mm)" = "#7AD151", "Medium (5-15 mm)" = "#21908C",
                 "Large (>15 mm)" = "#3B0F70")

# Fishery Bulletin figure rules: one sans-serif size for every label, no bold or italic, no
# background grid, no box around graphs (axis lines and ticks only), panel letters in bold Times
# New Roman, slightly larger, inside the upper left of each panel.
FONT_PT  <- 8
TAG_PT   <- 11
SANS     <- "Arial"
SERIF    <- "Times New Roman"
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = FONT_PT, base_family = SANS) +
  theme(text = element_text(size = FONT_PT, colour = "black"),
        axis.text = element_text(size = FONT_PT, colour = "black"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = FONT_PT), legend.text = element_text(size = FONT_PT),
        legend.title = element_text(size = FONT_PT), strip.text = element_text(size = FONT_PT),
        plot.title = element_text(size = FONT_PT, face = "plain"),
        strip.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.3), legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.height = unit(8, "pt")))

# A panel letter inside the upper-left corner, on a white box so it reads over any background.
panel_letter <- function(lab) {
  annotate("label", x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = lab, hjust = -0.25, vjust = 1.25,
           family = SERIF, fontface = "bold", size = TAG_PT / .pt,
           fill = "white", label.size = 0, label.padding = unit(1.5, "pt"))
}
```

Tables built by `01_data.Rmd`.

```{r read}
records <- read_csv(file.path(dir_derived, "cobia_records.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(size_class = factor(size_class, levels = SIZE_LEVELS))
lengths <- read_csv(file.path(dir_derived, "lengths.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(size = factor(size, levels = SIZE_LEVELS))
effort  <- read_csv(file.path(dir_derived, "effort.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

gulf <- records %>%
  filter(lon >= BOX$lon[1], lon <= BOX$lon[2], lat >= BOX$lat[1], lat <= BOX$lat[2])

# Numerator for any rate: the same gears and sorted status the effort pool is built from.
rates <- gulf %>% filter(gear %in% c("Bongo", "Neuston"), sort_ist %in% SORTED)
```

Bathymetry, isobaths and coastline, used by the three maps.

```{r basemap}
b <- getNOAA.bathy(BOX$lon[1], BOX$lon[2], BOX$lat[1], BOX$lat[2], resolution = 1, keep = TRUE,
                   path = dir_derived)
bathy <- as.xyz(b) %>% set_names(c("lon", "lat", "z")) %>% filter(z <= 0)
iso <- as.contour(rast(as.xyz(b), type = "xyz", crs = "EPSG:4326"),
                  levels = c(-200, -1000, -2000, -3000)) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>% st_set_crs(4326) %>% mutate(depth_m = -level)
land <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") %>% st_make_valid() %>%
  st_crop(st_bbox(c(xmin = BOX$lon[1], xmax = BOX$lon[2],
                    ymin = BOX$lat[1], ymax = BOX$lat[2]), crs = st_crs(4326)))
# Maps keep a neat line; the journal asks for a north arrow and a scale bar in km on every map.
map_frame <- list(coord_sf(xlim = BOX$lon, ylim = MAP_LAT, expand = FALSE), labs(x = NULL, y = NULL),
                  annotation_north_arrow(location = "tr", height = unit(18, "pt"),
                                         width = unit(12, "pt"), pad_x = unit(4, "pt"),
                                         pad_y = unit(4, "pt"),
                                         style = north_arrow_orienteering(text_size = FONT_PT,
                                                                          text_family = SANS)),
                  annotation_scale(location = "br", unit_category = "metric", width_hint = 0.2,
                                   text_cex = FONT_PT / 12, text_family = SANS,
                                   height = unit(3, "pt"), pad_x = unit(6, "pt"),
                                   pad_y = unit(6, "pt"), bar_cols = c("black", "white")),
                  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.line = element_blank(),
                        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3)))
```

Catch rates count larvae and effort from the same samples, which here are sorted bongo and neuston
deployments. Places are compared only within the months when both were sampled, because the
surveys do not cover the same areas in every month.

```{r excluded}
sprintf("off-gear or unsorted, kept on the map but out of every rate: %d records, %.0f larvae",
        nrow(gulf) - nrow(rates), sum(gulf$n_total) - sum(rates$n_total))
```

# Distribution

This map shows every record in the study area, colored by the size class that made up most of each
tow. It shows catches only, not catch rates, which come later.

```{r dist-numbers}
count(gulf, size_class)
gulf %>% slice_max(n_total, n = 3) %>% select(date, lat, lon, gear, n_total, n_meas)
```

Among tows with cobia, the median held one larva and 79% held one or two, but a neuston tow
off the Mississippi River delta on 8 June 2012 held 232, and the next station sampled that day held
38. That whole sample was sorted, so the count was not inflated by an aliquot correction. Symbol
sizes are binned, because on a continuous scale that one tow would make every other tow look small.

```{r main_distribution, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.6}
# Sorted bongo or neuston deployments at stations where no gear caught cobia.
no_cobia <- effort %>% filter(!v_c_p %in% records$v_c_p) %>%
  filter(lon >= BOX$lon[1], lon <= BOX$lon[2], lat >= BOX$lat[1], lat <= BOX$lat[2]) %>%
  distinct(lon = round(lon, 2), lat = round(lat, 2))
sprintf("stations with no cobia: %d deployments, %d distinct positions",
        sum(!effort$v_c_p %in% records$v_c_p), nrow(no_cobia))
p_dist <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = bathy, aes(lon, lat, fill = z), interpolate = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#6A93BF", high = "#EEF4FA", name = "Depth (m)",
                      labels = function(x) -x, breaks = c(0, -3000, -6000),
                      guide = guide_colourbar(order = 3, barwidth = unit(48, "pt"),
                                              barheight = unit(6, "pt"))) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(iso, depth_m == 200), colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(iso, depth_m > 200), colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.2,
          linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_sf(data = land, fill = "grey85", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = DWH, aes(lon, lat), shape = 8, size = 2.6, stroke = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = DWH$lon + 0.3, y = DWH$lat - 0.45, label = "DWH", size = FONT_PT / .pt, family = SANS, hjust = 0) +
  # stations searched with no cobia, as background for where larvae were absent
  geom_point(data = no_cobia, aes(lon, lat, colour = "No cobia"), size = 0.35, alpha = 0.6,
             shape = 16, show.legend = TRUE) +
  # smallest drawn last so they are not buried under the commoner medium tows
  geom_point(data = gulf %>% filter(!is.na(size_class)) %>%
               arrange(desc(as.integer(size_class)), desc(n_total)),
             aes(lon, lat, size = n_total, colour = size_class), alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(SIZE_COLS, "No cobia" = "grey30"), name = "Most of the tow",
                      breaks = c(SIZE_LEVELS, "No cobia"), drop = FALSE) +
  scale_size_binned(breaks = c(1, 5, 20, 100), range = c(1.2, 6.5), name = "Larvae per tow",
                    nice.breaks = FALSE) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = c(3.6, 3.6, 3.6, 1), alpha = 1)),
         size = guide_bins(order = 2, override.aes = list(colour = "grey45"))) +
  map_frame +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#EEF4FA"), legend.box = "horizontal",
        legend.box.just = "top", legend.spacing.x = unit(10, "pt"))
p_dist
```

# Season

This section uses only shelf stations from 1982 to 2016, so every month covers the same area and the
same years. Across the whole Gulf, the mix of shelf and deep-water effort changes from month to
month, and June and July sampling ended in 2016 while September sampling continued.

```{r season-rates}
recs <- rates  %>% filter(sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M, year %in% SERIES)
eff  <- effort %>% filter(sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M, year %in% SERIES)
cpue <- recs %>% count(month, wt = n_total, name = "n_larvae") %>%
  complete(month = 1:12, fill = list(n_larvae = 0)) %>%
  left_join(eff %>% count(month, name = "n_tows"), by = "month") %>%
  mutate(per_100 = if_else(n_tows > 0, 100 * n_larvae / n_tows, NA_real_),
         month_lab = factor(month.abb[month], levels = month.abb))
write_csv(cpue, file.path(dir_derived, "cpue_by_month.csv"), na = "")
cpue %>% select(month_lab, n_larvae, n_tows, per_100)
```

September has more sorted shelf tows than any other month, so raw counts make it look like a second
spawning peak. That peak disappears once counts are divided by effort.

The June peak also does not come from where sampling took place. On the Texas--Louisiana shelf
alone, which was sampled in every month, the difference between June and other months is larger.

```{r season-fixed-area}
tx <- effort %>% filter(region == "Texas-Louisiana shelf", year %in% SERIES) %>%
  count(month, name = "tows") %>%
  left_join(rates %>% filter(region == "Texas-Louisiana shelf", year %in% SERIES) %>%
              count(month, wt = n_total, name = "larvae"), by = "month") %>%
  mutate(rate = round(100 * coalesce(larvae, 0) / tows, 1))
tx %>% filter(month %in% c(5:9)) %>% select(month, tows, larvae, rate)
```

Catch rates peak in June, but the share of small larvae peaks in May. This fits larvae spawned in or
before May rather than a spawning peak in June. About two thirds of larvae were measured, so each
bar is split by the size composition of the larvae measured in that month.

```{r main_season, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3.2}
mix <- lengths %>% inner_join(select(recs, v_c_p_s_cat, month), by = "v_c_p_s_cat") %>%
  count(month, size, name = "n_meas") %>%
  group_by(month) %>% mutate(share = n_meas / sum(n_meas)) %>% ungroup()

p_season <- cpue %>% select(month, month_lab, per_100) %>% inner_join(mix, by = "month") %>%
  ggplot(aes(month_lab, per_100 * share, fill = size)) +
  geom_col(colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = SIZE_COLS, name = NULL, drop = FALSE,
                    guide = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = substr(month.abb, 1, 1), drop = FALSE) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.key.size = unit(8, "pt"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = FONT_PT)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cobia larvae per 100 sorted\nshelf tows, 1982-2016")
p_season
```

# The two shelves

Cobia in spawning condition are caught on the west Florida shelf, so the low number of larvae there
has to be checked against effort from the same season rather than read from an annual map. Only
about 12% of west Florida shelf tows were in June and July, compared with 26% on the
Texas--Louisiana shelf, because the summer survey works west of 88 W. This comparison therefore
uses only June and July.

```{r shelf-cells}
peak_eff  <- effort %>% filter(month %in% PEAK)
peak_recs <- rates  %>% filter(month %in% PEAK)
CELL <- 0.5
cell <- function(x) mutate(x, cx = floor(lon / CELL) * CELL + CELL / 2,
                              cy = floor(lat / CELL) * CELL + CELL / 2)
cells <- cell(peak_eff) %>% count(cx, cy, name = "n_tows") %>%
  left_join(cell(peak_recs) %>% group_by(cx, cy) %>%
              summarise(n_larvae = sum(n_total), .groups = "drop"), by = c("cx", "cy")) %>%
  mutate(n_larvae = coalesce(n_larvae, 0), per_100 = 100 * n_larvae / n_tows,
         searched = n_tows >= 10)
sprintf("cells with >=10 June-July tows: %d; of those with no cobia: %d",
        sum(cells$searched), sum(cells$searched & cells$n_larvae == 0))
```

```{r main_shelf_maps, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.4}
frame <- list(geom_sf(data = filter(iso, depth_m == 200), colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.3),
              geom_sf(data = land, fill = "grey85", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.2),
              map_frame, theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white")),
              theme(plot.title = element_text(size = FONT_PT, face = "plain")))
p_eff <- ggplot() + geom_tile(data = cells, aes(cx, cy, fill = n_tows)) +
  scale_fill_distiller(trans = "log10", palette = "Blues", direction = 1,
                       name = "Sorted June-July\ndeployments", breaks = c(1, 10, 100)) +
  frame + ggtitle("June-July sampling")
p_rate <- ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = filter(cells, searched, n_larvae == 0), aes(cx, cy), fill = "grey88") +
  geom_tile(data = filter(cells, n_larvae > 0), aes(cx, cy, fill = per_100)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "sqrt", option = "viridis", direction = -1,
                       name = "Cobia larvae per\n100 deployments", breaks = c(10, 100, 300)) +
  frame + ggtitle("June-July catch rate")
p_eff | p_rate
```

Effort is counted as one deployment per gear per station. Larvae are matched to effort by both
station and gear, because matching by station alone would count a tow's larvae in both the bongo
and the neuston rows and double the rate. Confidence intervals come from resampling tows with
replacement 2000 times (a bootstrap). In June and July, 219 of the 3298 Texas--Louisiana tows
caught cobia, and one tow held 232 of the 874 larvae. A Poisson interval treats each larva as an
independent catch, so with counts like these it gives intervals that are much too narrow.

```{r shelf-rates}
tow_catch <- peak_recs %>% filter(year %in% SERIES) %>%
  mutate(gear_class = if_else(gear == "Neuston", "Neuston", "Bongo")) %>%
  group_by(v_c_p, gear_class) %>% summarise(n = sum(n_total), .groups = "drop")
set.seed(7)
boot_ci <- function(x, n = 2000) quantile(replicate(n, 100 * mean(sample(x, replace = TRUE))),
                                          c(0.025, 0.975))
reg <- peak_eff %>% filter(!is.na(region), year %in% SERIES) %>%
  select(v_c_p, gear, region) %>%
  left_join(tow_catch, by = c("v_c_p", "gear" = "gear_class")) %>%
  mutate(n = coalesce(n, 0)) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(tows = n(), larvae = sum(n), rate = 100 * mean(n), pct_tows_with = 100 * mean(n > 0),
            ci = list(boot_ci(n)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lo = map_dbl(ci, 1), hi = map_dbl(ci, 2), .keep = "unused")   # both limits from one set of resamples
write_csv(reg, file.path(dir_derived, "shelf_comparison.csv"))
reg
```

The two shelves were also similar in station depth, gear mix, and years sampled, so the difference
does not come from differences in what was sampled.

```{r shelf-controls}
peak_eff %>% filter(!is.na(region), year %in% SERIES) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(years = n_distinct(year), depth_med = round(median(sta_depth_m)),
            depth_q1 = round(quantile(sta_depth_m, .25)),
            depth_q3 = round(quantile(sta_depth_m, .75)),
            pct_bongo = round(100 * mean(gear == "Bongo")), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r main_shelf_bar, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 3.4}
p_bar <- ggplot(reg, aes(reorder(str_remove(region, " shelf"), -rate), rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#0072B2", colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2, width = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(y = hi, label = sprintf("%d tows\n%.0f larvae", tows, larvae)),
            vjust = -0.3, size = FONT_PT / .pt, family = SANS, lineheight = 0.95) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.28))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Larvae per 100 shelf tows,\nJune-July 1982-2016")
p_bar
```

# Size

```{r size-tables}
by_depth <- lengths %>%
  inner_join(select(gulf, v_c_p_s_cat, sta_depth_m, month), by = "v_c_p_s_cat") %>%
  filter(sta_depth_m > 0)
by_depth %>% mutate(where = if_else(sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M, "shelf", "off-shelf")) %>%
  group_by(where) %>% summarise(n = n(), median_mm = median(length_mm),
                                median_depth_m = round(median(sta_depth_m)))
by_depth %>% filter(month %in% 4:10) %>% count(month, size) %>%
  group_by(month) %>% mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n))) %>%
  select(-n) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = size, values_from = pct)
```

```{r main_size_depth, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3.4}
p_size <- ggplot(by_depth, aes(sta_depth_m, length_mm, colour = size)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = SIZE_COLS, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(10, 30, 100, 300, 1000, 3000)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = SHELF_M, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "Station depth (m, log scale)", y = "Larval length (mm)")
p_size
```

There is no strong reason for the 5 mm cut-off for small larvae, so the shelf result is checked
across several cut-offs. The share caught on the shelf falls slowly as the cut-off rises and larger
larvae that have drifted farther are included, which is expected, and it never reverses.

```{r explore_size_cutoff}
map_dfr(c(3, 3.2, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5), function(cut) {
  keep <- lengths %>% group_by(v_c_p_s_cat) %>%
    summarise(hit = any(length_mm <= cut), .groups = "drop") %>% filter(hit)
  g <- gulf %>% filter(v_c_p_s_cat %in% keep$v_c_p_s_cat, !is.na(sta_depth_m))
  tibble(cut_mm = cut, larvae = sum(lengths$length_mm <= cut), records = nrow(g),
         pct_shelf = round(100 * mean(g$sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M)))
})
```

# Day and night

Catch rates are higher at night. Larvae may avoid the net in daylight, or they may stay deeper by
day and rise to the surface at night. The two explanations predict different patterns. If larvae
avoid the net, the largest larvae should show the biggest day-night difference, because they see
and swim better. If larvae move up at night, the neuston net, which samples only the top half meter,
should catch more at night, while the bongo net, which samples the whole water column, should catch
about the same by day and by night.

```{r diel-table}
diel <- lengths %>%
  inner_join(rates %>% filter(!is.na(night)) %>% select(v_c_p_s_cat, gear, night),
             by = "v_c_p_s_cat") %>%
  count(gear, night, size, name = "larvae") %>%
  left_join(effort %>% filter(!is.na(night)) %>% count(gear, night, name = "tows"),
            by = c("gear", "night")) %>%
  mutate(per_100 = 100 * larvae / tows) %>%
  select(gear, size, night, per_100) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = night, values_from = per_100, names_prefix = "n") %>%
  transmute(gear, size, day = round(nFALSE, 2), night = round(nTRUE, 2),
            ratio = round(nTRUE / nFALSE, 2)) %>% arrange(gear, size)
write_csv(diel, file.path(dir_derived, "diel_by_gear_size.csv"))
diel
```

Neuston nets caught 3 to 9 times more larvae at night, while bongo nets caught small and medium
larvae at about the same rate by day and by night (ratios of 1.09 and 1.07). This is the pattern
expected if larvae move up to the surface at night. The neuston night-to-day ratio also falls with
larval size, from 8.8 to 3.3, which is the opposite of what net avoidance predicts. The bongo values
for large larvae (0.01 and 0.05 per 100 tows) rest on four larvae and are not interpreted.

```{r explore_diel, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.2}
p_diel <- diel %>% pivot_longer(c(day, night), names_to = "tod", values_to = "per_100") %>%
  ggplot(aes(size, per_100, fill = tod)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2, width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ gear, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(day = "#FDE725", night = "#3B528B"), name = NULL,
                    labels = c(day = "Day", night = "Night")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("<5", "5\u201315", ">15")) +
  labs(x = "Larval length (mm)", y = "Measured larvae per 100 deployments")
p_diel
```

Early trawl surveys sampled mostly by day, and this changed around 1995. Between 1982-1994 and
1995-2016, June and July shelf rates rose both by day (1.4 to 7.5 larvae per 100 tows) and by night
(16.1 to 74.2). Daytime sampling therefore does not explain the rise by itself. The share of night
tows also rose, from 22% to 38%, and the mix of surveys changed over the series. The archive cannot
separate these changes from a real change in abundance, so no trend over years is plotted.

```{r diel-era}
era <- effort %>% filter(!is.na(night), month %in% PEAK, sta_depth_m > 0,
                           sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M, year %in% SERIES) %>%
  mutate(era = if_else(year < 1995, "1982-1994", "1995-2016")) %>%
  count(era, night, name = "tows") %>%
  left_join(rates %>% filter(!is.na(night), month %in% PEAK, sta_depth_m > 0,
                               sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M, year %in% SERIES) %>%
              mutate(era = if_else(year < 1995, "1982-1994", "1995-2016")) %>%
              count(era, night, wt = n_total, name = "larvae"), by = c("era", "night")) %>%
  mutate(larvae = coalesce(larvae, 0), per_100 = round(100 * larvae / tows, 1))
write_csv(era, file.path(dir_derived, "diel_by_era.csv"))
era
```

# Temperature

Ditty and Shaw (1992) described Gulf cobia larvae by the surface temperature at capture. They found
85% of their 76 larvae at 25 to 30 degrees, with a mean of 28.2 and a range of 24.2 to 32.0.
Temperature is the one variable where the archive can compare larvae with the conditions sampled,
because `STAREC` has a surface reading for nearly every station. The station table has no salinity,
so their salinity result cannot be checked here without another table.

The temperature at which larvae are caught is not a preference. Sampling is seasonal, so warm water
is sampled more than it would be across the full year. The comparison below is therefore against the
temperatures of all tows, not against the Gulf as a whole.

```{r temp-table}
temp_tows <- effort %>% filter(!is.na(temp_surf))
temp_pos  <- rates %>% filter(!is.na(temp_surf)) %>% uncount(n_total)

bind_rows(
  tibble(set = "All sorted tows",   t = temp_tows$temp_surf),
  tibble(set = "Larvae",            t = temp_pos$temp_surf)) %>%
  group_by(set) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = round(mean(t), 1), median = round(median(t), 1),
            min = round(min(t), 1), max = round(max(t), 1),
            pct_25_30 = round(100 * mean(t >= 25 & t <= 30), 1), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r explore_temp, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 3.2}
p_temp <- bind_rows(
  tibble(set = "All sorted tows", t = temp_tows$temp_surf),
  tibble(set = "Larvae",          t = temp_pos$temp_surf)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(t, after_stat(density), fill = set)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, position = "identity", alpha = 0.55,
                 colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("All sorted tows" = "grey60", "Larvae" = "#21908C"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Surface temperature (°C)", y = "Density")
p_temp
```

# Figures for submission

Each figure is saved as its own file, in PDF and as a 600 dpi TIFF, as the journal requires. Widths
match the printed page (7 in for full width, 3.5 in for one column) so that 8 pt labels print at
8 pt. All seven figures are exported and numbered in the order they appear in the Results. Figures 4
and 6 repeat Tables 2 and 3 and can be dropped to meet the limit of one figure per four pages of
text. Captions must spell out DWH (Deepwater Horizon wellhead) and the isobaths.

```{r journal-figures}
dir_journal <- file.path(dir_fig, "journal")
dir.create(dir_journal, showWarnings = FALSE)
# The macOS PDF device embeds system fonts (Arial, Times New Roman); the CRAN build's cairo_pdf
# does not find them there. Elsewhere cairo_pdf does.
pdf_device <- if (capabilities("aqua")) {
  function(filename, width, height, bg = "white", ...)
    grDevices::quartz(type = "pdf", file = filename, width = width, height = height, bg = bg)
} else grDevices::cairo_pdf
save_fig <- function(p, name, w, h) {
  ggsave(file.path(dir_journal, paste0(name, ".pdf")), p, width = w, height = h,
         device = pdf_device)
  ggsave(file.path(dir_journal, paste0(name, ".tif")), p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 600,
         device = ragg::agg_tiff, compression = "lzw")
}
diel_letters <- tibble(gear = c("Bongo", "Neuston"), lab = c("A", "B"))

save_fig(p_dist + theme(legend.box = "vertical", legend.box.just = "left",
                         legend.spacing.y = unit(2, "pt"), plot.margin = margin(2, 12, 2, 2)),
         "fig1_distribution", 7, 5)   # legends stacked to fit the 7 in page width
save_fig(p_season, "fig2_season", 5, 2.6)
save_fig((p_eff + panel_letter("A")) / (p_rate + panel_letter("B")), "fig3_june_july_maps", 7, 7.6)
save_fig(p_bar, "fig4_shelf_rates", 3.5, 3)                 # repeats Table 2; candidate to drop
save_fig(p_size, "fig5_size_depth", 3.5, 2.8)
save_fig(p_diel + geom_label(data = diel_letters, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = lab),
                             inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = -0.25, vjust = 1.25, family = SERIF,
                             fontface = "bold", size = TAG_PT / .pt, fill = "white",
                             label.size = 0) +
           theme(strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0.5)),
         "fig6_day_night", 7, 3)   # repeats Table 3; candidate to drop
save_fig(p_temp, "fig7_temperature", 3.5, 2.8)
list.files(dir_journal)
```

# Numbers for the text

Numbers quoted in the Results that are not shown elsewhere in this document.

## Catch by gear

All standard deployments, 1982-2024.

```{r text-gear}
all_tows <- effort %>% select(v_c_p, gear, night) %>%
  left_join(rates %>% group_by(v_c_p, gear) %>% summarise(n = sum(n_total), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("v_c_p", "gear")) %>%
  mutate(n = coalesce(n, 0))
all_tows %>% group_by(gear) %>%
  summarise(tows = n(), larvae = sum(n), per_100 = round(100 * mean(n), 2),
            pct_tows_with = round(100 * mean(n > 0), 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pct_of_larvae = round(100 * larvae / sum(larvae), 1))
all_tows %>% filter(!is.na(night)) %>%
  group_by(gear, night) %>% summarise(tows = n(), per_100 = round(100 * mean(n), 1), .groups = "drop")
sprintf("deployments with cobia: %d of %d", sum(all_tows$n > 0), nrow(all_tows))
```

## Against Ditty and Shaw (1992)

Ditty and Shaw (1992) reported 98% of larvae in June to September and 75% at stations shallower than
100 m (median 50 m). Every larva in the study area is counted here, as in their study, so these are
shares of the catch, not catch rates.

```{r text-ditty-shaw}
gulf %>% summarise(
  larvae = sum(n_total),
  pct_may_sep = round(100 * sum(n_total[month %in% 5:9]) / larvae, 1),
  pct_jun_sep = round(100 * sum(n_total[month %in% 6:9]) / larvae, 1),
  pct_under_100m = round(100 * sum(n_total[sta_depth_m < 100]) / larvae, 1),
  median_depth_m = round(median(rep(sta_depth_m, n_total))),
  records_off_shelf = sum(sta_depth_m > SHELF_M),
  larvae_off_shelf = sum(n_total[sta_depth_m > SHELF_M]))
count(gulf, month, wt = n_total, name = "larvae")
```

## The shelf comparison, sensitivity checks

The June and July comparison of the two shelves is repeated without the two largest catches, for
1995-2016 only, by time of day, and by gear. These confidence intervals resample whole cruises,
because tows on the same cruise share weather, water conditions, and crew.

```{r text-shelf-robustness}
shelf_tows <- peak_eff %>% filter(!is.na(region), year %in% SERIES) %>%
  select(v_c_p, gear, region, year, night) %>%
  left_join(tow_catch, by = c("v_c_p", "gear" = "gear_class")) %>%
  mutate(n = coalesce(n, 0), cruise = substr(v_c_p, 1, 5))   # vessel + cruise number

shelf_rate <- function(d, case) d %>% group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(rate = 100 * mean(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = region, values_from = rate) %>%
  transmute(case, tx_la = round(`Texas-Louisiana shelf`, 1), w_fl = round(`West Florida shelf`, 1),
            ratio = round(`Texas-Louisiana shelf` / `West Florida shelf`, 1))   # from unrounded rates
bind_rows(
  shelf_rate(shelf_tows, "all"),
  shelf_rate(filter(shelf_tows, rank(-n, ties.method = "first") > 2), "without the 2 largest catches"),
  shelf_rate(filter(shelf_tows, year >= 1995), "1995-2016"),
  shelf_rate(filter(shelf_tows, night %in% FALSE), "day"),
  shelf_rate(filter(shelf_tows, night %in% TRUE), "night"),
  shelf_rate(filter(shelf_tows, gear == "Neuston"), "neuston"),
  shelf_rate(filter(shelf_tows, gear == "Bongo"), "bongo"))

set.seed(7)
shelf_tows %>% group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(cruises = n_distinct(cruise), pct_night = round(100 * mean(night, na.rm = TRUE)),
            ci = list(quantile(replicate(2000, {
              by_cruise <- split(n, cruise)
              100 * mean(unlist(by_cruise[sample(names(by_cruise), replace = TRUE)]))
            }), c(0.025, 0.975))), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lo = round(map_dbl(ci, 1), 1), hi = round(map_dbl(ci, 2), 1), .keep = "unused")
```

# Checks

Each check states what should be true, calculates it, and shows both values so the comparison can
be seen rather than reduced to pass or fail.

## Extraction reproduces from the raw table

Counts taken directly from `ISARWK` should equal the counts carried through the pipeline.

```{r check-extraction}
isarwk <- read_csv("data/raw/seamap/ISARWK.csv", col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                   show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal") %>%
  rename_with(~ str_remove(.x, "^\ufeff"))
ALIQ_MULT <- c("1/1" = 1, "1/2" = 2, "1/4" = 4, "1/8" = 8)

raw <- isarwk %>% filter(str_detect(toupper(TAXON), "^RACHYCENTR")) %>%
  mutate(n = (coalesce(as.numeric(MEAS), 0) + coalesce(as.numeric(NOT_MEAS), 0)) *
             coalesce(ALIQ_MULT[ALIQUOT], 1))

tibble(quantity    = c("records", "larvae after aliquot correction", "sub-sampled records"),
       from_raw    = c(nrow(raw), sum(raw$n), sum(raw$ALIQUOT != "1/1")),
       in_pipeline = c(nrow(records), sum(records$n_total), sum(records$aliquot != "1/1"))) %>%
  mutate(agree = from_raw == in_pipeline)
```

A taxon match that is not anchored to the start of the name would also pick up *Poromitra
megalops*, a melamphaid with the same species name. The two lists below should be identical.

```{r check-taxon}
tibble(anchored   = paste(sort(unique(raw$TAXON)), collapse = "; "),
       unanchored = isarwk %>% filter(str_detect(toupper(TAXON), "RACHYCENTR")) %>%
                      pull(TAXON) %>% unique() %>% sort() %>% paste(collapse = "; "))
```

## Station join

Every record should carry a station, and positions and dates should be possible.

```{r check-join}
tibble(quantity = c("records without a station", "latitude range", "longitude range",
                    "date range", "duplicated catalogue keys", "records outside the study box"),
       value = c(as.character(sum(is.na(records$lat))),
                 sprintf("%.1f to %.1f N", min(records$lat), max(records$lat)),
                 sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", min(records$lon), max(records$lon)),
                 sprintf("%s to %s", min(records$date), max(records$date)),
                 as.character(sum(duplicated(records$v_c_p_s_cat))),
                 as.character(nrow(records) - nrow(gulf))))
```

## Larvae and effort come from the same samples

Effort includes only sorted bongo and neuston deployments, so a larva caught any other way has no
matching effort. These records are left out of every rate.

```{r check-excluded}
gulf %>%
  mutate(why = case_when(!gear %in% c("Bongo", "Neuston") ~ paste("gear:", gear),
                         !sort_ist %in% SORTED            ~ "not flagged sorted",
                         TRUE                             ~ "in the rates")) %>%
  count(why, wt = n_total, name = "larvae")
```

Recalculating the monthly larva counts from scratch, with all four filters applied, should give the
same numbers used in the rates.

```{r check-numerator}
tibble(source = c("rebuilt here", "used in the monthly rates"),
       larvae = c(gulf %>% filter(gear %in% c("Bongo", "Neuston"), sort_ist %in% SORTED,
                                  sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M,
                                  year %in% SERIES) %>% pull(n_total) %>% sum(),
                  sum(cpue$n_larvae)))
```

## Lengths

Length coverage is uneven and lowest in the largest tows, so size classes in those tows rest on the
fewest measurements.

```{r check-lengths}
tibble(quantity = c("larvae measured", "larvae counted", "coverage",
                    "tows holding >10 larvae", "of those, under half measured",
                    "length range", "measured exceeds counted",
                    "size classes do not sum to measured"),
       value = c(sum(gulf$n_meas, na.rm = TRUE), sum(gulf$n_total),
                 sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * sum(gulf$n_meas, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(gulf$n_total)),
                 sum(gulf$n_total > 10),
                 sum(gulf$n_total > 10 & gulf$n_meas / gulf$n_total < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
                 sprintf("%.1f to %.1f mm", min(lengths$length_mm), max(lengths$length_mm)),
                 sum(gulf$n_meas > gulf$n_total, na.rm = TRUE),
                 sum(gulf$n_small + gulf$n_mid + gulf$n_big != gulf$n_meas, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
         as.character())
```

## Depth

Station depth is recorded in fathoms and converted to meters. An independent bathymetry dataset
checks the conversion. The two should agree closely, and a missed conversion would show as a
constant offset on the log scale.

```{r check-depth}
chk <- gulf %>% filter(sta_depth_m > 0)
chk$etopo_m <- -terra::extract(rast(as.xyz(b), type = "xyz", crs = "EPSG:4326"),
                               as.matrix(chk[, c("lon", "lat")]))[, 1]
chk <- filter(chk, etopo_m > 0)
tibble(stations = nrow(chk),
       correlation_log_depth = round(cor(log10(chk$sta_depth_m), log10(chk$etopo_m)), 3),
       median_ratio = round(median(chk$sta_depth_m / chk$etopo_m), 2),
       disagree_over_fourfold = sum(chk$sta_depth_m / chk$etopo_m > 4 |
                                    chk$sta_depth_m / chk$etopo_m < 0.25))
```

## Does the seasonal peak hold under the controls?

The survey does not sample the same places or the same hours in every month. If the June and July
peak came from either, it should weaken when the area is held fixed or when day and night tows are
analyzed separately. It does not weaken in either case.

```{r check-season-controls}
tod <- effort %>% filter(!is.na(night), sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M,
                         year %in% SERIES) %>%
  count(month, night, name = "tows") %>%
  left_join(rates %>% filter(!is.na(night), sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M,
                             year %in% SERIES) %>%
              count(month, night, wt = n_total, name = "larvae"), by = c("month", "night")) %>%
  mutate(rate = 100 * coalesce(larvae, 0) / tows)

tibble(control = c("all Gulf shelf, pooled", "Texas-Louisiana shelf only",
                   "day tows only", "night tows only"),
       june_july = c(max(cpue$per_100[cpue$month %in% PEAK]),
                     max(tx$rate[tx$month %in% PEAK]),
                     max(tod$rate[tod$month %in% PEAK & !tod$night]),
                     max(tod$rate[tod$month %in% PEAK & tod$night])),
       september = c(cpue$per_100[cpue$month == 9], tx$rate[tx$month == 9],
                     tod$rate[tod$month == 9 & !tod$night],
                     tod$rate[tod$month == 9 & tod$night])) %>%
  mutate(across(june_july:september, ~ round(.x, 1)), ratio = round(june_july / september, 1))
```

## Does the shelf difference hold?

West Florida has a much smaller share of its tows in the spawning months, which is why a comparison
across all months was misleading. In June and July the two regions are similar in station depth,
gear, and years sampled, so the difference does not come from differences in sampling.

```{r check-shelf-controls}
effort %>% filter(!is.na(region), sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(shelf_tows = n(), pct_in_june_july = round(100 * mean(month %in% PEAK)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(effort %>% filter(!is.na(region), month %in% PEAK, year %in% SERIES) %>%
              group_by(region) %>%
              summarise(years = n_distinct(year), depth_median = round(median(sta_depth_m)),
                        pct_bongo = round(100 * mean(gear == "Bongo")), .groups = "drop"),
            by = "region") %>%
  left_join(reg %>% select(region, rate, lo, hi) %>%
              mutate(across(rate:hi, ~ round(.x, 1))), by = "region")
```

## Why no interannual trend is fitted

Early trawl surveys sampled mostly by day, which changed in the mid-1990s. If that alone caused the
rise in catch rates, only the day rate should increase across the change. Both increased, the day
rate about 5.4-fold and the night rate about 4.6-fold. Daytime sampling is therefore not the only
explanation, and the share of night tows and the mix of surveys also changed. The archive cannot
separate these from a change in abundance, so no trend is fitted.

```{r check-trend}
era %>% select(era, night, tows, larvae, per_100) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = era, values_from = c(tows, larvae, per_100)) %>%
  mutate(fold_change = round(`per_100_1995-2016` / `per_100_1982-1994`, 1))
era %>% group_by(era) %>% summarise(pct_night = round(100 * sum(tows[night]) / sum(tows)), tows = sum(tows))
```

## Surface temperature sentinels

`TEMP_SSURF` is entered as zero when no reading was taken. Left in, these zeros would lower the mean
and add false cold-water records. The raw column is compared with the filtered one.

```{r check-temp}
raw_t <- read_csv(file.path("data/raw/seamap", "STAREC.csv"),
                  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                  show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal") %>%
  rename_with(~ str_remove(.x, "^\ufeff")) %>%
  transmute(t = as.numeric(TEMP_SSURF))

tibble(check = c("stations in STAREC", "temperature recorded", "zero or below 5",
                 "above 36", "kept"),
       n = c(nrow(raw_t), sum(!is.na(raw_t$t)), sum(raw_t$t < 5, na.rm = TRUE),
             sum(raw_t$t > 36, na.rm = TRUE),
             sum(raw_t$t >= 5 & raw_t$t <= 36, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

## June and July sampling ends in 2016

Records run to 2024, but plankton sampling on the summer trawl survey stopped after 2016. A monthly
comparison that ignores this would compare June and July from one set of years with September from
another.

```{r check-series-end}
effort %>% filter(month %in% PEAK, sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M) %>%
  count(year, name = "june_july_shelf_tows") %>%
  filter(year >= 2013) %>%
  full_join(tibble(year = 2013:max(gulf$year)), by = "year") %>%
  arrange(year) %>%
  mutate(june_july_shelf_tows = coalesce(june_july_shelf_tows, 0L))
```

## Station times are read in their recorded zone

`TIME_ZN` changes from local time to GMT over the series. If the conversion is correct, the share of
tows classed as night should stay about the same from decade to decade rather than jump when the
recording practice changes.

```{r check-time-zone}
effort %>% mutate(decade = 10 * (year %/% 10),
                  zone = recode(as.character(time_zn), "1" = "EST", "2" = "EDT", "3" = "CST", "4" = "CDT",
                                "5" = "AST", "6" = "ADT", "8" = "GMT", .default = "other")) %>%
  group_by(decade) %>%
  summarise(tows = n(), pct_gmt = round(100 * mean(zone == "GMT")),
            pct_local = round(100 * mean(zone %in% c("EST", "EDT", "CST", "CDT", "AST", "ADT"))),
            pct_night = round(100 * mean(night, na.rm = TRUE)),
            no_time = sum(is.na(night)), .groups = "drop")
```
